articleTitle: Design of a self-charging electric vehicle with embedded multiple natural energy sources
abstract: In the era of automation and wireless connectivity. There is advancement in industry of automobile and urge to develop the sector EV’s. As EV’s can be multi purposely used for different sectors to grow. In agricultural sector, EV’s can be true gift to industry to reduce input cost and bringing advancement in farming technology. Additionally, it will reduce pollution in nature and can be easily maintained by the owner. In this paper, an EV that will be having AVR sensors to advance the technology used in farming. After the completion of our models, we will be able to check soil moisture, humidity level in specific region and PH levels of soil remotely. Also, this model of EV is completely ecofriendly in nature as it is using power generated by solar and wind energy at particular levels. The main reason for making Electric vehicles (EV) is i) to avoid overuse of limited petroleum resources ii) High-cost of transportation iii) the year the oil supply ends in 2040 according to the prediction iv) High focus on decreasing air pollution and noise pollution to make an environment friendly design.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of Cascode Current reuse low power Operational transconductance amplifier
abstract: Demand for the low-power operational transconductance amplifier (OTA) circuit designs are increasing in analog systems with a major focus on reducing power consumption with desired overall performance. However, achieving low-power operation with improved values of other performance metrics is a crucial task in CMOS technology. In this work, current reuse cascode OTA is deigned in $0.18 \mu \mathrm{m}$ CMOS technology which works at $\pm 0.5 \mathrm{~V}$. The reported OTA delivers power dissipation of 0.337 $\mu \mathrm{W}$, gain of $70.13 \mathrm{~dB}$, gain-bandwidth of 25 kHz, input referred noise of $0.192 \mu \mathrm{V} / \sqrt{} \mathrm{Hz}$, output voltage swing of -365.1 mV to 365.1 mV, common mode rejection ratio of $98 \mathrm{~dB}$, power supply rejection ratio of $80.53 \mathrm{~dB}$, and Figure of merit of 1261.12. Further, the proposed OTA delivers positive and negative slew rates of $1.55 \mathrm{kV} / \mathrm{s}$ and $1.48 \mathrm{kV} / \mathrm{s}$, respectively. The proposed current reuse cascode OTA is projected to be used in medical acquisition systems.

articleTitle: CNTFET-based design of low power charge pump technique-based voltage multiplier
abstract: This study presents an effective approach for designing voltage multiplier using CNTFET devices based on charge pump and low power consumption for devices used in renewable energy systems. This method has been developed analytically and evaluated using experimental measurement and the simulation through 32nm CNTFET technology. The technique allows to the designers to determine the number of stages that improves performance of the given input voltage and reduces the power consumed during conversion. In the proposed work, the applied input voltage is 97 mV, and the resultant output voltage is 1000 mV, which is almost 10 times better than the applied input voltage resulting in a highly optimum multiplier result. The power consumed for conversion is 5.631 nW, which is extremely low in contrast to earlier studies, and the produced output is significant through the use of CNTFET devices.

articleTitle: A Review on Emerging Tunnel FET Structures for High-speed and Low-power Circuit Applications
abstract: Tunnel FET is found to be a prominent candidate to address the various issues like short channel effects, thermionic limitation, which are dominant in MOSFET. It has grabbed the attention of researchers because of its BTBT tunneling mechanism across the source-channel interface which reduces the short-channel effects and improving the S<inf>AVG</inf> lower than 60mV/Dec. Although TFET mitigates the SCE’s and $\mathrm{SS}_{\mathrm{AVG}}$ but ON-current and ambipolar conduction are the roadblocks that degrades the performance. This paper presents a detailed survey on various structures (techniques) introduced by the researchers to address the performance improvement in Tunnel FET.

articleTitle: Impact of Doping Variation on the Performance of Sb2S3 based Solar Cell using Device Simulations
abstract: Antimony sulphide (S$\mathrm{b}_{2}\mathrm{S}_{3}$) is a promising material used as photovoltaic (PV) absorber for high PV performance owing to non-toxicity. However, the device performance is still limited by unoptimized doping density in S$\mathrm{b}_{2}\mathrm{S}_{3}$ absorber. Therefore, in this work, SCAPS-ID tool is used to design the $\mathrm{S}\mathrm{b}_{2}\mathrm{S}_{3}$ based PV device. The effect of different acceptor doping variation (NA) from 10<sup>10</sup> to 10<sup>19</sup> c$\mathrm{m}^{-3}$ has been studied and analyzed. The proposed device structure, which has been designed using device simulations, consists of several layers, namely ITO, ZnO, Zn(O,S):N, SnO<inf>2</inf>, and S$\mathrm{b}_{2}\mathrm{S}_{3}$. This multilayered structure has been carefully constructed with the intention of improving the device’s performance and efficiency. After doing the variation, the device performance is optimized at 10<sup>1S</sup> c$\mathrm{m}^{-3}$ and achieved higher PV parameters: Jsc of 14. 1SmA/cm<sup>2</sup>, Voc of 1.1 V, FF of 76.41% and PCE of 10.S9%. The obtained results of this whole study provide new vision for the development of device.

articleTitle: Subsuming AI, IoT and Big Data in Smart Farm Practices
abstract: Farm Practices are relatively high now days the work efficiency on agriculture development so far is increasing as compare to initial era, Initial signs of the projected profound alteration of daily life & agricultural supply chains are already apparent, are indeed supply and distribution networks for food, fiber, or bio-energy. In this article, we discuss industrial agriculture’s current state as well as the lessons we’ve learned from industrialized farm level patterns, industrialized agricultural production methods, and the industrialized agri-food supplier. In order to achieve Agriculture 4.0, artificial intelligence, big data, & blockchain are addressed. The proposed work supports continuous monitoring and management of an agricultural farm through remote observation of the framework for agriculture-based farm activities in the context of IoT, AI, and other technologies. We concentrate particularly on the main research problems and uses of these developing technologies in the agriculture industry. The readership of this paper, especially industry practitioners, is intended to be introduced to fresh research prospects. It is anticipated that the development of basic IoT and other technological tools for agricultural production would usher in a new era of connected, reliable, & productive agriculture.

articleTitle: Ensemble Learning strategy in modeling of future generation nanoscale devices using Machine Learning
abstract: In semiconductor industry, conventional method of device characteristics analysis using TCAD based simulation is sometimes difficult. TCAD based device simulation gives the insight of the device with inclusion of detailed device physics with required analytical calculations. But with similar device structure having change in technology node, performance prediction using TCAD simulation is time consuming and proper expertise is necessary to run the simulations. However, machine learning based prediction algorithms may outperform traditional methods in this regard. But machine learning models should be trained with sufficient data. As the TCAD simulation generated dataset is relatively small in size, performance of the model based on only one algorithm may yield unsatisfactory result. One of the solution is to use ensemble learning strategy. Though several ensemble learning methods exists, this paper discusses the opportunities of using Stacking as the Ensemble Learning method. Here, the model uses heterogeneous algorithms in base-models and regression algorithm in metamodel state, for accurate prediction of performance in Junctionless FinFETs. Results obtained clearly indicates the reduction in prediction error.

articleTitle: A Review of Low-Power Static Random Access Memory (SRAM) Designs
abstract: The growing demand for low-power static random access memory (SRAM) cells in Internet of Things (IoT) devices has led to the development of various SRAM cell topologies that minimize power consumption while maintaining performance and stability. In this paper, we have analyzed various SRAM designs based on different parameters, such as power dissipation, delay, area, energy, and stability. It is observed that 6T SRAM cell, consisting of six transistors, is the most widely used topology due to its simplicity and low area requirements. However, larger cells such as 8T,9T, and 10T have been developed to improve stability and reduce power consumption, although they require more area. It has been observed8 T work better for read delay while 9T works better for 9 Scaling down SRAM cells to smaller feature sizes presents challenges in maintaining stability and reliability while minimizing power consumption.

articleTitle: Design and Modeling of a Label-free JLTFETBased Biosensor for Enhanced Sensitivity
abstract: This article discusses the operation of a Junctionless (JL) TFET as a biosensor for detecting various protein molecules. Due to JLTFET’s advantages over TFETs and JLFETs, a JLTFET-based biosensor is chosen. By carving cavities across the gates, the biomolecules are trapped. The performance of label -free biosensing with dielectric modulation has been investigated using the TCAD simulator. This paper also addresses the sensitivity to current and voltage. In addition, the effect of size, fill factor, and cavity location on the performance of biosensors is investigated in this work. This is simulationbased research of the dielectric modulation approach for detecting multiple proteins and amino acids. To obtain the expression for drain current, the analytical model for the proposed biosensor is solved. The sensitivity of biosensors based on JLTFET is on the order of 10<sup>13</sup>.

articleTitle: Optimizing Photovoltaic Performance of MASnPbI3 Perovskite Solar Cells through Layer Thickness Variations
abstract: Perovskite materials have gained significant interest in the field of the photovoltaic industry due to their superior power conversion efficiency, broad spectral response, flexibility, stability, and low-cost manufacturing. The bandgap of perovskite materials can be adjusted to improve solar cell efficiency. In this study, a perovskite-based solar cell (MASnPbI<inf>3</inf>) has been designed and investigated. The thickness of the perovskite layer has been varied in a simulator to determine the best performance of the cell. Results indicate that the MASnPbI<inf>3</inf> solar cell delivers optimum PV parameters at 300 nm thick MASnPbI<inf>3</inf>. The optimum performance of the cell is achieved in respect of photovoltaic characteristics: Voc: 0.96 V, Jsc: 35.93 mA/cm<sup>2</sup>, FF:7S.97 %, and PCE: 27.94 %. This makes the MASnPbI<inf>3</inf> solar cell a potential candidate of PV industry.

articleTitle: Design of An IoT Based Smart Medicine Box
abstract: Based on the Healthcare system, the project involves designing and developing medicine reminders and dispensing machines. In the current pandemic situation, nurses and doctors give patients medicines to reduce pain, boost their physical strength to fight with diseases, and maintain their health. The immune system will be strengthened, and symptoms will be reduced. A machine to take in the pharmaceutical doses for a complete month was created to save healthcare warriors’ lives when they are administering the medication to patients. The machine helps to ensure that there is no human contact between the patient and the caregiver, eliminating the risk of virus transmission. It also makes sure that medications are taken on time and monitored, which helps to ensure the patient’s health and safety. Additionally, regular meals and exercise routines can help patients better adhere to their medication schedules, ensuring that they take the correct dosages at the right times.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things Based Technological Advancement in Domain of Horticulture 4.0
abstract: Horticultural plants significantly contribute for both food and nutrition security in a vibrant way of life. Using the Internet of Things (IoT) and Artificial Intelligence (AI), for the quick growth of new things evaluated nearly in every sector, particularly in field of smart agriculture. Underneath the present climate changing situation, with a rising population and little farmland, agriculture, particularly horticulture, is facing mounting problems in meeting the diverse needs of modern everyday existence for that purpose the study highlights to improve current procedures for disease diagnosis, irrigation methods, growing conditions, maturation identification, or advertising. This study also focuses on the evolution of key parameters and the principles that drive them, as well as recent study innovations in horticulture crops which yields positive result in domain of horticulture. Lastly, it discusses how technological advances might be used in conjunction with transdisciplinary fundamental research to improve our knowledge and utilization of horticulture crops.

articleTitle: Analysis of Source, Drain and Gate Field Plated AlGaN/GaN Based HEMT for High Breakdown Voltage
abstract:
The rapidly-increasing operation frequency and power density in electrical power conversion systems require the synthesis of power electronics devices that surmount Sibased devices. AlGaN/GaN based HEMTs are remarkable in their demonstration of higher breakdown voltage, lower onstate resistance, higher switching frequencies and higher temperature capabilities (about 300 oC for GaN devices compared to 150<sup>o</sup> C of Si based devices). In high power devices, however, circuit designers suffer from having to employ sluggish and insensitive FETs which have poor transconductance and subthreshold slope values. In our proposed structure, we have found a solution to this issue, proposing a structure that provides excellent high-power performance in addition to being fast and sensitive. articleTitle: Enabling Technologies for Wildlife Conservation
abstract: Wildlife conservation has always been a majorconcern on a global scale, but with the advent of Industry 4.0, or the fourth Industrial Revolution, the use of smart, intelligent technology to safeguard biological wildlife has increased significantly. The technology also facilitates to monitor species and their habitat in novel ways. The paper reviews various methodologies of wildlife conservation using drones which includes radiotracking, GPS and Non- GPS transmitters, Unmanned aerial vehicles or Robotics aircrafts. The Artificial Intelligence reviews the methods including Convolutional Neural Network, Machine learning and Deep learning algorithms. Lastly, the paper demonstrates recommendation and the limitations which are possessed by various models of wildlife conservation and come up with different suggestions for the assurance of wildlife heritage effectively and efficiently. The current state of wildlife conservation is largely based on various technological models of Industrial revolution which was earlier continued by sociocultural conventional sources based on human intelligence only.

Author Keywords: deep learning and machine learning algorithms

articleTitle: Study on the impact of CuI as Hole Transport Layer (HTL) for CZTS-based Solar Cell
abstract: CZTS (copper zinc tin sulfide) is a promising candidate for solar cell applications. In this simulation-based work, the comparison of cell output variation is examined by considering the layer thickness as well as series and shunt resistances. When CuI is used as a hole transport layer (HTL), the Schottky barrier is reduced and efficiency is raised. The final optimized cell with CuI as the HT layer obtained a power conversion efficiency of 16.92%. The performance of the device was compared with and without HTL. The study’s findings pave the path for using CuI as an HTL for solar cell device production using CZTS.

articleTitle: Mechanical and Electrical Performance of Stretchable Honeycomb Interconnect with Aspect Ratio Variation
abstract: Structural design engineering of interconnects in flexible electronics is an interesting study to understand the signal integrity and transmission of a signal between multiple devices over a circuit layer under different types of mechanical stress. The geometric design of flexible interconnects makes an important role in understanding the device functionality and optimization over a layout area. In this work, we try to compare variation in uniaxial stretchability of honeycomb inspired stretchable interconnect along with serpentine interconnect for the same range of aspect ratios using finite element analysis (FEA). We will be investigating how doubling the aspect ratio of these two geometries changes the layout parameters. Von Mises Stress and electrical resistance of the wires are also evaluated. The interconnect structures are designed with copper film embedded in between the two layers of polyimide. The comparative study of nature-inspired honeycomb and meandered serpentine geometry gives an overview of realizing innovative wire designs for applications of in-plane stretchable circuits.

articleTitle: Comparative Performance between V/F and Rotor Flux-Oriented Controls of Induction Motor Drive
abstract: A comparison between the performances of two popular speed control techniques for three-phase induction motors are presented. The scalar control (also known as V/F control) of induction motors is widely used. But its performances under various operating conditions are not satisfactory. As a result, a vector control technique, i.e., a rotor flux-oriented control technique, is thought to improve its performance under different working states, allowing flexibility in various applications. Various tests are conducted using MATLAB-SIMULINK software, and results are provided that highlight the comparative performances between the control methods for induction motor drives. Superior parameters in speed and torque responses are noticed in case of rotor flux-oriented method.

articleTitle: Early Prediction of Cataract using Convolutional Neural Network
abstract: Cataract is one of the most common ocular diseases. It causes cloudy vision and vision loss in a vast number. In this paper, a convolutional neural network model has been proposed to detect cataract in the eyes. This model will help the patient and ophthalmologists with early and accurate cataract detection. This model is built on the VGG19 architecture having roughly three layers. At first, some pre-processing techniques have been applied to the image dataset. After pre-processing, the dataset is split into training and test dataset. The proposed model is trained with the pre-processed training dataset. The datasets for experimentation are downloaded from an online repository. A detailed analysis is done based on the predicted output and actual class label. The overall accuracy of the model is 97.47%.

articleTitle: A Temperature Compensated Beta-Multiplier Based Sub-1 V Voltage Reference Circuit for Low-Voltage Applications
abstract: A beta-multiplier based voltage reference circuit is proposed here that generates a reference voltage of $\approx$0.6V for low-voltage analog and mixed-signal applications. The circuit is designed in SCL 0.18 $\mu$m standard CMOS technology under 1.8 V power supply. The circuit offers a line regulation of 0.16% N over the range of 1.8 V to 3.5 V supply voltage variation. A stable response with a temperature coefficient of 42.5ppm/°C is obtained for temperatures varying between industry-standard temperature range of -40° C to +85° C. The proposed circuit offers a power supply rejection ratio (PSRR) of -42.1dB at lowfrequency range up to 1 MHz frequency. The circuit draws a total current of 19.47 $\mu$A from the power supply resulting in overall power consumption of 35.05 $\mu$W which is quite comparable with the very recent existing reported works.

articleTitle: 9T SRAM Cell for Computation-In-Memory Architectures: Proposal & Investigation
abstract: By keeping data-intensive applications into consideration, we have investigated the robustness of digital logic circuit design for Computation In-Memory (CiM) using 9T SRAM cells at 22 nm technology nodes. PVT analysis (Process corner, Voltage, and Temperature) is also presented to check the robustness of the circuit. We have proposed a latch-based sense amplifier and voltage reference for 9T SRAM-based CiM architecture. The proposed design is good for demonstrating the logical operation with the memory. A comparison of 250 nm technology against 22 nm is also demonstrated in this work for 9T SRAM-based CiM.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of 8× 8 SRAM Memory Array using 45 nm Technology at 100 MHz
abstract: The main goal of this paper is to build an 8 by 8-bit SRAM memory array using 45nm CMOS technology. The SRAM array is read by a 3-bit address using a 3-to-8 decoder. The SRAM cells are made to operate at 100 MHz Read & Write cycles with the least amount of power usage and the appropriate static noise margin. Through Cadence Virtuoso’s Analog-Design Environment, both the SRAM array and decoder are implemented, tested, and laid out using software models. (ADE).

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Aided Intelligent Framework for Condition Monitoring of Electrical Machinery
abstract: Single-phase induction motors (SPIM) are fairly efficiently employed in household devices and possess wide applications in the industrial system. Typically, current signature-analysis (CSA) based methods have been used for fault diagnosis, but not always been an efficient solution, especially for fractional kW SPIMs that may be replaced entirely iffaulty. This paper presents a deep learning (DL) based fault detection scheme of a SPIM which is in-service in household devices. The fault detection is done employing a wavelet based deep dense convolutional neural network (W-D2CNN), where several wavelets are used as convolutional filters for convolution operation. The convoluted feature maps are further passed through a proposed nonlinearity, i.e., SLReLU, for richer feature extraction. The uniqueness of the proposed method lies in the feature learning ability, where upper-and lower-layer features of the dense block fuse via concatenation operation. Also, the SL-ReLU has been designed to combine logarithmic function, softsign, and ReLU operation. The designed SL-ReLU minimizes the probability of convoluted output and gradient explosion, due to which training has been improved along with feature learning ability. Comprehensive results reveal the efficacy of the proposed work in terms of performance metrics with state-of-the-art DL frameworks using the same dataset. The proposed work can also be extendable to multiphase-induction machines or any other electrical device working in any environment for fault identification.

articleTitle: Design of DC-DC Boost Converter Using PFM Switching Technique
abstract: An efficient Power management block that utilizes Pulse Frequency Modulation for Thermal Energy harvested applications is presented. The following paper focuses on energy harvesting applications, specifically thermoelectric generation (TEG), which produces a voltage that acts as an input to DCDC boost converters. The small voltages generated by TEG are amplified by controlling the transistor (used in boost converter) using an efficient duty cycle through Pulse Frequency Modulation (PFM). PFM block includes a voltage divider, comparator, charge pump, filter, and VCO. These blocks control the transistors, there by enhancing the DC-DC boost converter’s overall efficiency. The Circuits were simulated using Cadence 180nm technology. An output voltage of approximately 900 mV was achieved with a relatively low input voltage of only 100 mV when the entire block was simulated.

articleTitle: Device Performance Analysis for Different Gate Locations in AlGaN/GaN HEMT by Silvaco Simulation
abstract: AlGaN/GaN-based high electron mobility transistors (HEMTs) with different gate locations have been simulated in Silvaco. The current-voltage analysis suggests that placing the gate nearer to the source results in a higher saturation current. This happens as the voltage nearer to the source is less than comparable to the drain. This causes lesser reverse bias across the gate metal-semiconductor junction. Thus a HEMT with gate contact near the source is very useful for high-power applications. At the same time, noise analysis of the devices suggests that the minimum noise figure, for the HEMTs where the gate contact is placed nearer to the source contact is higher than its counterparts. This creates some reliability issues in semiconductor devices. The possible reason behind such a phenomenon has also been discussed in thiswork.

articleTitle: Analysis of FDSOI-Negative Capacitance MOSFET with Respect to Different Oxide Thickness and Temperatures
abstract: Our research focuses on the study of Fully Depleted Silicon on Insulator Negative Capacitance Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor Field-Effect Transistors (FDSOI-NC-MOSFET) characteristics. This study aims to use ferroelectric material to improve the performance and efficiency of FDSOI Negative capacitance MOSFETs compared to conventional planar MOSFETs. Using TCAD software, FDSOI-NC-MOSFET is simulated and analyzed under various conditions and parameters (like Temperature, channel thickness, input supply voltages, and doping levels of the channel). Variations in these parameters will affect the operating region of the device, thereby the choice of parameters in achieving the best performance will depend on the operating conditions and device applications. NC-MOSFET with ferroelectric materials can obtain an acceptable ON/OFF current ratio by lowering the OFF current and can achieve an adequate subthreshold swing (SS). It is observed that the NC-MOSFET device has enhanced performance and transfer characteristics in comparison to planar MOSFET and is being studied further for various other parameter adjustments to reach a more optimal result. Later in this paper, a circuit-level design using NCMOSFET device is implemented and simulated in support of future circuit-level digital logic design applications.

articleTitle: Threshold Voltage Analysis of E-mode Recessed p-GaN Gate HEMT-A Simulation Based Study
abstract: In power-electronics applications or switching applications Normally-off AlGaN/GaN high electron mobility transistors (HEMTs) are needed with higher threshold voltage ($\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{t}\mathrm{h}}$) and high drain current (Id). Previously a lot of experiments have been done to propose emode HEMT structures by using several gate engineering techniques like recessed metal-gate HEMT, p-GaN gate HEMT and thin-barrier layer HEMT etc. This paper depicts a unique enhancement-mode recessed p-GaN gate HEMT structure with incorporating recess gate (p-GaN) engineering techniques which have unique advantages of all above proposed structures. Proposed results got up to 2. 7V of threshold voltage and by analyzing the band diagram, it is also observed that the triangular well at AlGaN/GaN interface is uplifted to 2. 54eV from the Fermi-level, which is significantly higher than p-GaN gate HEMT (only 0. 42SeV from the Fermi level). The proposed HEMT structure is simulated in Silvaco Atlas software version 5. 0.22.R by changing the parameters like x-mole fraction of the barrier layer, recess depth ($\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{d}}$), and doping concentration of p-GaN layer (NA). The trans-conductance graph is generated by Tony-plot tool available in the software.

articleTitle: Schottky barrier height modulation of Metal-WS2 contact by molecular doping technique
abstract: Determination of electrical transport property of the layered 2D TMDC material is fundamentally important to semiconductor device development. In this work the contact resistance ($\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{c}}$) at the junction of 2D Tungsten Disulfide and metal has been investigated. The W$\mathrm{S}_{2}-$metal interface suffers from poor electrical conductivity due to the formation of sulfur vacancies during the exfoliation process. The reported work shows a tendency to reduce the $\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{c}}$ and Schottky barrier height ofWS<inf>2</inf> after Cl doping. The conductivity of doped and undoped WS<inf>2</inf> thin films were studied and the $\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{c}}$ value was extracted from Transfer length (TLM) method. A reduction in contact resistance from 0.34 k$\Omega$ to 0.15 k$\Omega$ and SBH from 1.02 eV to 0. SeV has been noticed after doping.

articleTitle: Study on Effect of Si-SiO2 and SiGe-HfO2 to Design 8nm Double Gate MOSFET with Applications
abstract: In this research an 8 nanometer n-type Double Gate Metal Oxide Semiconductor Field Effect Transistor (DGMOSFET) has been demonstrated with two different semiconductors (Si and Si<inf>0.7</inf>Ge0.3) as substrate and oxide agent (SiO<inf>2</inf> and HfO<inf>2</inf>) as insulator. The electrical parameters such as Leakage Current, Drive Current, $\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{o}\mathrm{n}}$/$\mathrm{I}_{0\mathrm{f}\mathrm{f}}$ Ratio and Threshold Voltage are measured as well as also perform a comparison analysis with IRDS 2020 and existing literature. The proposed system is operated using optimal threshold voltage of 0. 35V and 0. 3SV respectively for Si and SiGe channel. The obtained drive current ($\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{o}\mathrm{n}}$) are 46.45X1$0^{-4}$A/$\mu$m and 65.17X1$0^{-4}$A/$\mu$m and obtained leakage current ($\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{o}\mathrm{f}\mathrm{f})}$ are 1.02SX1$0^{-10}$A/$\mu$m and 1.021X1$0^{-11}$A/$\mu$m respectively for Si-SiO<inf>2</inf> and SiGe-HfO<inf>2</inf> material composition at drain voltage ($\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{d}\mathrm{s}}$) of 0. 7V and gate voltage ($\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{g}\mathrm{s}}$) of 0 to 1 volt. The calculated $\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{o}\mathrm{n}}$/$\mathrm{I}_{0\mathrm{f}\mathrm{f}}$ values are 4.51SXI07 and 6. 3SX10S for Si-SiO<inf>2</inf> and SiGe-HfO<inf>2</inf> material composition respectively. An inverter circuit is configured from the proposed S nm DG-MOSFET with different materials.

articleTitle: An Offset-Fed T-Shaped Two-Port MIMO Antenna for 38 GHz 5G Millimeter-Wave band Applications
abstract: This paper represents an offset-fed T-shaped microstrip patch antenna for radiation of electromagnetic energy in a 38 GHz mm-wave band for fifth-generation (5G) wireless communication technology. Roger RT/5880 of size 12× 10mm with height h=0.254 mm is used having relative permittivity and loss tangent of 2.2 and 0.0009 respectively. The design comprises two conventional rectangular patches combined to form a T-like structure with offset feed for the 38 GHz band. The dimensions of rectangles are optimized to provide resonance at 38 GHz and can be useful in mobile infrastructure. The antenna provides an impedance bandwidth of 2.2 GHz with 8.04 dBi gain for the targeted band. The proposed antenna radiating EM wave is also analyzed for a 2-port MIMO configuration and provides microwave access. The elements are placed adjacent to each other without any decoupling structure. MIMO provides an isolation of more than 22dB in the frequency range of 37.1GHz to 39.3 GHz. It is also analyzed for diversity parameters with Envelope Correlation Coefficient at 38 GHz (ECC38) is less than 0.02, Diversity Gain(DG38) >9.999dB, Total Active Reflection Coefficient(TARC38) < zero dB, and Channel Capacity Loss(CCL38) of less than 0. 4b/s/Hz.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of EEPL and PPL Techniques in 18nm FinFET Technology
abstract: Pass Transistor Logic characterizes several logic families by eliminating redundant MOS transistors from the CMOS digital architecture. This logic can be effectively employed to construct the area and power efficient digital logic circuits. At ultra-scaled technology nodes, the performance of circuits based on CMOS technique gives degraded performance. In this work, one-bit adder circuit by using push-pull pass transistor logic (PPL) and energy economized pass transistor logic (EEPL) approaches are designed. FinFET 18nm technology has been used to perform the comparative analysis of these two approaches. The results show that the Power Delay Product (PDP) and Energy Delay Product (EDP) values of EEPL based on-bit adder are 563.13× 10<sup>-15</sup> and 2836. 51× 10<sup>22</sup>, respectively. While for PPL based design the PDP and EDP values are 7488.74× 10<sup>-15</sup> and 37638.4× 10<sup>22</sup>, respectively. EEPL based one-bit adder circuit design has demonstrated enhanced transient response in comparison to PPL based one-bit adder.

articleTitle: Significance of Emerging Technological Advancements in Transition of Green Economy
abstract: UNEP’s SDGs agenda 2030 focuses on the reduction of negative environmental impacts to achieve green economy. Industry 4.0 calls for energy efficient and clean energy technologies as a solution to reduce the impacts of global warming and climate change to achieve Sustainable Development Goals set by United Nations Environment Programme. United Nations Environment Programme is promoting green economy as an alternative solution to achieve sustainable development. Exponential technologies have a significant Role in achieving all the Sustainable Development Goals. United Nations Environment Programme in its report on ‘Technology and innovation’ has expected that by the year 2025, the market growth of technologies would be ${\$}$3.2 trillion. In this regard study covers the frontier technologies- Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning, the Internet of things (IoT), Big Data Analytics and Block chain. The present study is related to SDG 8 and 9. This paper analyzes the significance of technological advancements for green economy. The study analyzes that technological advancements have a significant Role in sustainable developmental aspects. Therefore, to attain green economy, there is a need to encourage research and innovation on energy and environment.

articleTitle: Low-power class-AB flipped source follower filter for voltage-sensitive applications
abstract: Low pass filter (LPF) architecture is an indispensable block of voltage-sensitive applications. However, designing a LPF which delivers low figure-of-merit (FOM) along with lowpower operation is crucial. The paper recommends a low-power quasi-floating gate (QFG) class-AB flipped source follower (FSF) LPF architecture based on QFG MOS technique. The proposed LPF architecture is designed in Cadence using BSIM3V3180 nm CMOS technology which works at 0.5 V, delivers gain of -4.5dB, bandwidth of 100 Hz, input referred noise of S6 $\mu \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{r}\mathrm{m}\mathrm{s}}$, total harmonic distortion of -50.26dB, input voltage range of100 m$\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{p}\mathrm{p}}$ at frequency of SO Hz, power of 0.056 nW. The proposed QFG class-AB FSF LPF is suitable candidate for voltage-sensitive applications such as geoenvironmental monitoring, biomedical and healthcare etc.

articleTitle: Intersubband effects on electron mobility in GaAs/ InxGa1-xAs Quantum well FET with asymmetric doping profiles
abstract: Authors analyze electron mobility, $\mu$ by taking asymmetric doping concentrations, varying nd1 in the substrate barrier and keeping nd 2 constant in the surface barrier. With increase in nd1, $\mu$ increases mostly dominated by ionized impurity (imp-) and alloy disorder (al-) scatterings for lowest subband occupancy and then by imp-scattering only when two subbands are occupied. At the starting of second subband, inter subband scattering triggers, causing drop in $\mu$. Mobility due to imp scattering ($\mu$<sup>imp</sup>) is governed by intra subband scattering rate while $\mu^{\text {al}}$ and $\mu$<sup>ir</sup> are governed by inter subband scattering rates. For well width $w=200 \unicode{0x00C5}, \mu$ enhances from $1.1 \times 10^{5} \mathrm{~cm}^{2} / \mathrm{V}$ s to $1.4 \times 10^{5} \mathrm{~cm}^{2} /$ Vs with increase in nd1 (from $0.1 \times 10^{18} \mathrm{~cm}^{-3}$ to $1.4 \times 10^{18} \mathrm{~cm}^{-3}$). At nd1 $=1.5 \times 10^{18} \mathrm{~cm}^{-3}$ second subband starts, leading to considerable drop in $\mu$ and thereafter with further increase in nd1, $\mu$ rises through intersubband effects. As well width increases, the drop in $\mu$ occurs at less value of nd1 and in fact for $w=400 \unicode{0x00C5}$ there is fully double subband occupied. The results of $\mu$ mediated through inter subband effects can help in analyzing the characteristics of the QWFET devices.

articleTitle: Design of Low Power, Low Noise with High Output Swing Preamplifier of Cochlear Implants
abstract: Cochlear implantation is a procedure that uses electrical stimulation in the auditory nerve system to restore partial hearing. In this work, a low-power, high-gain with high output swing preamplifier has been designed for a cochlear implant. Capacitive feedback topology is used along with the current scaling resistor to maintain the noise under the limit and to overcome the trade-off between noise and power. Simulations and post-layout analyses for the proposed preamplifier were done in Cadence Virtuoso using UMC 180 nm technology. In the proposed OTA, a maximum gain of 44.23 dB, total average power of l. 69$\mu$W, a phase margin of 45 degrees, and noise of 2.71 $\mu$V/sqrt(Hz) at 1 Hz are obtained. Also, we have analyzed the capacitive feedback closed loop OTA in which we have obtained a maximum mid-band gain of 43.75 dB, and bandwidth of22.55 Hz to 18.55 kHz.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Buried Gate Oxide based Negative Capacitance FinFETs
abstract: In the era of shrinking technology nodes and gate lengths, Negative Capacitance Fin Field-Effect Transistors (NC-FinFET) hold a one-sided dominance over the conventional structures, due to their superior gate electrostatics. However, the advancement of NC-FinFETs has been made possible by the enhanced device performance in terms of numerous engineering techniques. The following work proposes a novel NC-FinFET architecture in which the depth of the interfacial gate oxide (IGO) layer has been modified and examined with the help of $T C A D$ Sentaurus. Based on several short channel parameters, we have shown a comparison between the standard NC-FinFET, lowk spacer based NC-FinFET, and the projected FE-DE spacer NC-FinFET, by modifying the IGO thickness inside the channel. Additionally, we have shown the effect of side IGO thickness to realize the best configuration with the entire IGO depth inside the channel. In conclusion, this principle of buried IGO thickness seems motivating for low-power electronics.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Dielectrically Modulated Tunnel FET Embedded Nanocavity for BreastCancer Cells
abstract: This paper presents the design and simulation of Dielectrically Modulated Tunnel Field Effect Transistor embedded with dual nanocavities. The device has been simulated as a label free biosensor for cancer cell biomolecules. We have used Silvaco ATLAS model for all simulations of the device and we have find the performance parameters in the presence of different cancer cells biomolecules. We have analyzed the drain current, and sensitivity for the presence of different cancer cell biomolecules.

articleTitle: Truncated corner and slotted wearable textile multiband antenna for wireless
abstract: Wearable antennas perform important role in WBAN (Wireless Body Area Network). Wearable antennas can be embedded in garments, implanted in the user’s body and even tattooed on the skin. In this research paper, the textilebased multiband antenna is proposed for wearable applications. The proposed multiband antenna is designed on flexible substrate using cotton material and operates over frequencies 5. 6GHz, 7.4GHz and 9. 0GHz. Also, the top patch and bottom ground plane of the proposed antenna is designed using conducting silver shield material. The most important considerations for wearable antenna design is its portable size, gain, bandwidth, flexibility, and its biocompatibility with the human body. Here, the designed antenna is compact with dimensions of 50 x60x2 mm3. Also, the designed antenna exhibits appreciable reflection coefficient values of -24.70dB, - 21.14dB & -35.48dB at 5. 6GHz, 7. 4GHz and 9. 0GHz respectively. Also, the designed antenna has good performance with a gain of 6. 76dBi, 6.19dBi & 4. 47dBi, bandwidth of 556MHz, 636MHz & 682MHz and good flexibility. Moreover, it is observed that the simulated antenna with using silver shielded material exhibits better voltage standing wave ratio, surface distribution current and radiation efficiency. The prototype antenna is fabricated and measurement results are achieved at resonant frequencies of 6. 0GHz, 7.2GHz and 8. 8GHz with reflection coefficients -20.26dB -15.62dB and 18. 90dB. The proposed multiband wearable antenna is suitable for Wi-Fi, Radio altimeters, 5G and Satellite applications.

articleTitle: Dielectric-Pocket based Multi-channel Nanowire Field Effect Transistor for High-speed Operations
abstract: The brain of electronic devices are MOSFETs, such as Silicon-Dielectric pocket packed-Gate All Around/Nanowire (Si-DPP-GAA). Because of their unique biomedical and electrical characteristics, FETs are an essential component for the future generation of electronic systems. The article illustrates the characteristics of Si-GAA-DPP-multi-channel cylindrical MOSFET designed in nether scientific nodes. The proposed structure can be regarded as one of the leading models in the Nanowire-MOSFET lineage thanks to improvements in gate leakage current ($\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{o}\mathrm{f}\mathrm{f}}$), Subthreshold-Swing (SS), and DrainInduced-Barrier-Lowering (DIBL). The study encompasses the effect of variation in channel length from 10nm to 25nm on the SS and DIBL. The improved OFF-state current with higher electrostatic integrity is paving its way towards future evolution of high speed and low power memories based on CMOS technology.

articleTitle: Phase Transition Material Modulated Hyper FET for Digital Applications
abstract: In this paper, a Phase Transition Material Modulated Hyper-FET has been proposed for Digital Applications. It has been examined by implementing a Spice model of Phase Transition Material with the source of 32nm MOSFET and later a comparison is drawn with 32nm MOSFET. In our proposed device, ISO-IOFF transfer characteristics and Output Characteristics of 32nm HyperFET reveal approximately 104 times higher ON current. The metallic resistivity, insulating resistivity, insulating to metallic current density, metallic to insulating current density, and geometry of Phase Transition Material are varied to study the effect on transfer characteristics of Hyper-FET in order to optimize the parameters for proper operation of the device.

articleTitle: An approach for modeling propagation delay of a subthreshold inverter incorporating DIBL effect
abstract: The paper investigates the impact of Drain Induced Barrier Lowering (DIBL) on the propagation delay of subthreshold CMOS inverters. The authors analyze the subthreshold behavior of the inverter using LTSpice simulations and show that the DIBL effect impacts the transistor characteristics and the circuit performance. The paper demonstrates that neglecting the DIBL effect leads to inaccurate estimates of the inverter propagation delay, which can cause errors in the circuit design. By considering the DIBL effect, the paper proposes a new model to accurately calculate the inverter propagation delay in the subthreshold region. The proposed model that takes into account the DIBL effect has been shown to accurately predict the propagation delay over a wide range of conditions and technology parameters.

articleTitle: Temperature Sensitive Analysis of Junctionless Nanowire Ferroelectric Field Effect Transistor (JNFe- FET) for Enhanced Analog Performance
abstract: In this manuscript, we propose a study that evaluates the effect of temperature on junctionless nanowire ferroelectric field effect transistor (JNFe-FET). In the present study, it is verified that JNFe-FET exhibits better performance over conventional Junctionless nanowire field effect transistor (JN-FET) in terms of drain current, transconductance and output conductance at various temperatures (100K, 200K,300K, 400K, and 500K). In JNFe-FET, due to the negative capacitance phenomenon, internal voltage amplification takes place which leads to a reduction in subthreshold swing (below 60 mV/decade, Boltzmann Tyranny). The effect of negative capacitance diminishes with an increase in temperature. Electric potential and electric field have also been studied for the proposed model. The simulations have been performed using the ATLAS 3-D device simulator.

articleTitle: An Exploration of Photovoltaic Performance of the Rb2SnI6 using DFT and SCAPS-1D
abstract: Perovskite with organic and lead-based cations work well, but their toxicity and stability have hindered their commercialization. In this study, we used WIEN2k software to perform first-principles calculations based on density functional theory (DFT) framework to determine the optical and electronic properties of the proposed perovskite material Rb<inf>2</inf>SnI<inf>6</inf> to be used as an absorber for solar cells (SCs). The DFT results for band gap, carrier mobility, effective densities, and absorption spectra are put into the SCAPS (Solar Cell Capacitance Simulator)-lD software to estimate how well the proposed perovskite solar cell (PSC) structure (FTO/TiO<inf>2</inf>/Rb<inf>2</inf>SnI$\epsilon$/PTAA/Au) will work as a photovoltaic device. TiO<inf>2</inf> and PTAA are employed as electron and hole transport materials respectively. We have also investigated the device performance with different organic hole transport layers (HTLs). The optimized series resistance ($\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{s}}$) of 1 $\Omega$. cm<sup>2</sup>, Shunt resistance ($\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{s}\mathrm{h}}$) of 1$ 0^{4}\Omega$. cm<sup>2</sup>, defect density of 10<sup>13</sup>c$\mathrm{m}^{-3}$, and thickness of 0.8 $\mu$m was used for the final simulation. The proposed device after optimization exhibits a $\mathrm{J}_{\mathrm{s}\mathrm{c}}$ of 40.4 mA/c$\mathrm{m}^{2},\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{o}\mathrm{c}}$ of 0. 72V, FF of 79.7 %, and PCE of 22.4 %. We also investigated the quantum efficiency (QE) of the proposed PSCs. Combination of this computational and simulation analysis of non-toxic Rb<inf>2</inf>SnI6 double perovskite (DP) reveals that it is advantageous for potential SC applications.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Performance of Electrostatically Doped Double POLO PERC Solar Cell through Metal Silicides
abstract: Passivated emitter and rear cell (PERC) solar cell technology has garnered significant attention in the photovoltaic (PV) industry due to its ability to enable mass production with minimal losses. However, contact recombination losses remain a limiting factor for device performance. To mitigate these losses, a double-POLO (polysilicon on oxide) contact approach utilizing polysilicon on oxide is employed to serve as passivating contacts. As part of this study, a PERC device by using double POLO is designed through Silvaco-TCAD simulator. Additionally, another technique i.e., electrostatically doping (ED) is used as an alternative to physical-doping without poly-Si layer. Further, this proposed study investigates the influence of metal silicides on rear surface viz $\operatorname{ErSi}_{0.25}(3 \mathrm{eV}), \mathrm{Ti}_{5} \mathrm{Si}_{3}(3.71 \mathrm{eV}), \mathrm{YbSi}_{2}(3.95$ eV) on front surface and ErSi ${}^{1}.7(5.4 \mathrm{eV}), \mathrm{WSi}_{2}$ (5.2 eV), Pt<inf>2</inf>Si $(5.17 \mathrm{eV})$. To evaluate the proposed device, various $P V$ parameters, J-V curve and EQE curve are analyzed. The results indicate that optimized metal silicides with low WF of ErSi $0_{0.25}(3 \mathrm{eV})$ on the front surface and for rear side, high WF of $\mathrm{ErSi}_{1.7}(5.4 \mathrm{eV})$ lead to superior performance. The proposed device achieved optimized higher $P V$ parameters viz. $J_{S C}(41.02$ $\left.\mathrm{mA} / \mathrm{cm}^{2}\right)$, Voc $(0.735 \mathrm{~V})$, FF (80.73 %), and PCE(24.34 %). These results demonstrate the potential of silicide-based double-POLO devices and can serve as a foundation for future advancements in the performance of PERC device.

articleTitle: Digitalization Transformation: Essence of Virtual Reality Indulging in the Mental Health of People
abstract: Virtual reality as a powerful tool of Industry 4.0 is working alongside traditional therapy methods for the treatment of mental health problems as an effective treatment strategy for mental conditions. It has extensive uses custom- tailored for treatment of various mental issues. In this study, the review of the use of Virtual Reality in the treatment of mental health disorders is examined and changes in the procedure have been suggested in accordance with the problems faces in therapeutic procedures. The respective benefits arising from the use of such technology in the treatment are also studied. The study also contributes to how the psychiatric health of the person is affected by the alteration of the markers during the treatment procedure done in a Virtual environment and the factors responsible for such change. The combined usage of the technology and traditional methods hasresulted in a positive outcome. Based on the examination of the technology within the mental health sector, the study concludes that VR technology with slight modifications and in conjunction with traditional therapy methods can be integrated into the mental health sector with higher efficiency to improve the treatment procedure of various mental health diseases.

articleTitle: IoT Based Smart Work Jacket for Coal Miners

authors.preferredName: N. D. B. Rudra Prasada Rao

abstract: Engineer is the person who is always interested in providing best solution to any kind of complex problem. In this paper we find the solution to the issues faced by the workers who work in the coal mines. There hazardous places like mines, factories, dumps etc. get unhealthy too frequently because of the pollution in the air and breathing poisonous gases while working. As an Engineer, we had an idea to make a device that can monitor the health conditions of the person, temperature of the body of a person and pollution in the air and alerts them when it is not in favourable conditions. So, a device which will be attached to smart jacket takes the reading while the worker is working in those conditions. The data can monitor and transfer by the long-range module and alerts the person working as well as the manager of the conditions.

articleTitle: IoT Based Monitoring of Environment in a Smart Hydroponic System
abstract: The amount of usable agricultural land is gradually diminishing as industrialization progresses. To address the challenges of unsuitable soil in certain areas, hydroponic farming has emerged as a viable solution for producing fruits, flowers, and vegetables. This soilless gardening technique is especially useful in large greenhouse operations for growing exotic crops. We cannot grow all the plants and vegetables in extreme weather conditions. Few species cannot tolerate this kind of extreme condition. In this manuscript we have designed a methodology in which we can grow plants and vegetables indoors. We have used a hydroponics system in this manuscript. Hydroponics is a type of system in which we grow plants and vegetables without using soil. We have used microcontrollers and sensors to make this system fully automated. We have implemented things for the analysis of the growth of plants in hydroponics technology.

articleTitle: Cyber Physical System Role in Stock Market
abstract: The stock market is a system that provides a platform between investors and companies and provides a strong foundation for the proper functioning of the economy. Stock market act as a source of fmance and evaluation tool which is responsible for overall growth and analysis of the economy. The present work focuses on the benefit of technology on the stock market and the effect of technologies on ease and accessibility towards investors. The goal of our study is to analyze the role of the fourth industrial revolution in the financial market and how it can benefit the investors. The articles included in this study are chosen based on the following criteria: journal and review articles, Englishlanguage publications, articles that only addressed ‘‘stock market ‘‘technologies’’, ‘‘finance’’, ‘‘blockchain ‘‘artificial intelligence and ‘‘economy’’. The result of this study confirms that technology is consistently converting the face of the stock market and the stock market and technology are unquestionably essential components in fostering economic growth. Overall based on the study it is examined and concluded that technologies have created an effective impact on the stock market by facilitating smoothness, costeffectiveness, effective stock exchange for traders and investors. This study will be helpful in making an informed investment decision and can help investor for making predictive and less sentimental analysis.

articleTitle: IOT Based Precision Agri-Bot
abstract: Agriculture is the heritage and accounts for the majority of India’s GDP, earning it the nickname ‘‘Golden Bird The high labor cost is a major factor in distributing seeds and ground level water scarcity. And without a doubt, we can solve these problems by employing a variety of agriculture techniques that will increase precision agriculture in a closed field. The most important benefit to us is the availability of an abundance of sunlight. Our robot i.e., Agri-Bot is implemented with a camera connected to a laptop/PC through a Wi-Fi network as an IoT based robot. It consists of servo motor and ploughing tool to seed distributer and watering the field. It is also equipped with bolometer (IR sensor) and HR-SR04 (Ultrasonic sensor). Ultrasonic sensor works as a proximity sensor to avoid obstacles and IR to sense the boundary of the working field. The Agribot is made up of an Arduino UNO ATmega328p microcontroller which is an epicenter is our robot.

articleTitle: Design of Secure Reversible Select, Cross and Variation (RSCV) Architecture in Quantum Computing
abstract: The principles of quantum physics serve as the foundation for the power of quantum computing technologies. Since these events lack a classical counterpart, conventional computers cannot provide comparable outcomes. Future studies are dominated by the rapidly expanding field of quantum technology application. Its popularity has increased as a result of several unique features that are missing in traditional domains. Real-time quantum computing makes it easy to design and apply unique quantum layouts on accessible quantum computing platforms. Quantum machines claim to possess high computing power in the field of cryptography. Expertise in communication security has helped this area grow significantly over time. A novel method of data encryption termed SCV (select, cross, and variation), based on input data halves swapping, is shown here utilizing the reversible quantum logic. Using a variety of quantum gates, we created this technique in this study in IBM Quantum. The developed method is applied to several quantum simulators; the quality is compared concerning frequency, no. of qubits, run time, and quantum volume (QV).

articleTitle: Single Layer Design of Dual Banyan Network Using Quantum-Dot Cellular Automata
abstract: A multistage and internally non-blocking communication architecture called a dual banyan network distributes the inputs based on the receiver’s port address with an internally non-blocking technique. It interprets the port address or output address as a string. The creation of a singlelayer dual banyan network utilizing QCA is demonstrated in this work. This study achieves a 4× 4 dual banyan network using a crossbar switch as a key-building piece. Device area, latency, and logic gates are taken into consideration when judging the designs. To ensure design accuracy, theoretical parameters, and simulation data have been compared. Using the QCADesigner tool, all the designs are put into practice.

articleTitle: Input Variable Bypass or IVB Technique for Logic Functions Simplification
abstract: In this article a novel simplification technique has been proposed. The input variable bypass technique or IVB technique is proposed for logic function simplification, which is used to minimize the logic functions very easily. If any output equation is simplified from the truth table and this output equation is the function of a few variables, then others output equations can be simplified from the previous output function. One can be neglect or bypass the used input variable for logic simplification.

articleTitle: Resonant Method for Determining the Dielectric Characteristics of A Mixture of Small Dispersed Bulk Materials at Ka-Band
abstract: In this research work, a resonator method is developed for studying the dielectric properties of a mixture of bulk materials made of cement and sand at Ka-band. The dielectric constant and loss tangent of studied mixture are experimentally obtained and then allow achieving the dielectric characteristics of a dielectric resonator made as a mixture of cement and sand, and is excited using whispering gallery modes (WGMs). Moreover, it is found that the proposed measurement technique presents very high resolution with concentration dependences of the dielectric characteristics of developed mixture.

articleTitle: An on-demand charging schedule utilizing multiple mobile charging vehicles for WRSNs
abstract: Low battery energy has always been a serious challenge for sensor nodes (SNs) in wireless sensor networks (WSNs). WSNs are experiencing energy constraints, which can be addressed by the wireless charging of SNs. The charging approach employed with these rechargeable SNs is called a ‘‘wireless rechargeable sensor network’’ (WRSN). While numerous research initiatives have been made to enhance WRSN charging performance, little has been done to overcome the scheduling issue associated with the mobile charging vehicles (MCVs) constrained capacity. By ‘‘MCV scheduling problem we imply how efficiently the capacity of numerous MCVs may be employed so that the SNs’ energy demands are met with the fewest number of MCVs. We suggest an ondemand charging approach to address this research gap. When compared to the other schemes, the simulation results show that the proposed scheme can obtain good results in terms of MCV tour length and SN survival ratio, proving the effectiveness of the scheme.

articleTitle: Design of a Catenary Shaped Multiband-MIMO Antenna for Ultra-Wideband Applications
abstract: For multiband applications, A planar multiple inputs multiple outputs (MIMO) antenna is introduced for Satellite communication, Infrastructure and wireless technologies employ Radio frequency spectrum. Good isolation and a lower value of correlation without the usage of decoupling structures are the key attributes of an antenna. Two-element patch radiator in a catenary shape with a circular aperture constitutes the suggested structure. At the centre of the ground plane, a rectangular slot is engraved for bandwidth enhancement. The monopoles are positioned orthogonally for interference-free radiation and improved diversity performance. the suggested structures with total dimensions are $52 \times 33 \times 1.6 \mathrm{~mm}^{3}$ on an FR4 substrate, and their impedance-matched using a 50-ohm microstrip line. Additionally, the antenna MIMO properties of impedance bandwidth, correlation coefficient, reflection coefficient, radiation characteristics, diversity gain, and peak gain are analyzed. With a low correlation coefficient of less than 0.3 and a peak gain of 2-4 dBi, the proposed structure has a 2-12 GHz bandwidth. Better isolation is demonstrated by the developed design, which is also wideband operated and compact without compromising anything.

articleTitle: Low Lead All-Inorganic Hybrid Perovskite: A Study of Interface Defects using SCAPS-1D
abstract: Hybrid perovskites are promising materials for photovoltaic applications due to their long diffusion length, high absorption coefficient, longer carrier lifetime, and adjustable bandgaps. However, the toxic nature of lead in hybrid perovskites is still a concern for the environment. In this work, a low-lead, all-inorganic perovskite material (CsP$\mathrm{b}_{0.625} Z \mathrm{n}_{0.375}$IC1<inf>2</inf>) is proposed as the absorber layer. The addition of zinc reduces lead content, and all-inorganic materials have better stability against temperature and moisture variations. TiO<inf>2</inf> is selected as the electron transport layer (ETL) and Spiro-MeOTAD as the hole transport layer (HTL) to efficiently collect the charge carriers at electrodes. The proposed design (TiO<inf>2</inf>/CsP$\mathrm{b}_{0.625} Z \mathrm{n}_{0.375}$IC1 2/SpiroMeOTAD) has been verified in the SCAPS-ID simulator under the influence of interface defect variation. Results show a decrease in current density and quantum efficiency with an increase in interface defect density at the ETL/absorber layer interface. It is observed that the current density decreases from 33.02 mA/cm<sup>2</sup> to 29.97 mA/cm<sup>2</sup> with an interface defect density of 1 x10<sup>10</sup> c$\mathrm{m}^{-2}$ and 1 x10<sup>1S</sup> c$\mathrm{m}^{-2}$, respectively. However, for the absorber layer/HTL interface, the current density remains constant at 33.02 mA/cm<sup>2</sup> on variation of defect density from 1 x10<sup>10</sup> c$\mathrm{m}^{-2}$ to 1 x10<sup>1S</sup> c$\mathrm{m}^{-2}$.

articleTitle: High Gain Multistage CMOS Amplifier Design at 45nm technology node
abstract: Analog design is still a challenge for designer working at lower technology node due degradation in devices and circuit performance and increased short channel non ideal effects. Medical equipment needs a high gain low noise amplifier frequently in medical data acquisition and signal processing. CMOS differential amplifiers are suitable choice for designer due its high value of gain, noise margin and CMRR. Multiple stages of amplifiers further improve gain but at the cost other analog performance. Use of low and high VT transistors are preferred for the transistor connected to input signal and load respectively. Multiple stages of PMOS load are also improves the overall gain with the increase in number transistors. To achieve high gain self-bias operational transconductance amplifiers are suitable choice with higher W/L ratio of PMOS at output stage amplifier. In this paper, CMOS based high gain self-bias double-stage and triple stage amplifiers have been designed at 45nm technology node using Cadence Virtuoso. DC and transient analysis are carried out for performance evaluation to find suitable amplifier topology and circuit schematic.

articleTitle: FPGA-based Design of a Fault Injector for Binarized Convolutional Neural Network
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is used in every modern system with the advancement of technology. Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is a popular and advanced AI technique for feature extraction and is widely used in safety-critical embedded systems. Fault tolerance must be a significant aspect of such embedded systems. To test various algorithms related to fault tolerance, the system must have a faulty condition. The Fault injection technique is used in the embedded system for testing purposes. This technique introduces faults into the system to ensure erroneous behaviour of that system. This paper presents a fault injection model to incorporate faults into the binarized convolution Neural Network (BCNN). It may help researchers to reduce the effort of fault-tolerant CNN simulation. An FPGA-based design has also been developed to validate the proposed model.

articleTitle: Sub-threshold Swing Analysis for NC-TFET in Low-Power Biomedical Applications
abstract: In the 21<sup>st</sup> century as the technology became more and more advanced the demand for the low power devices is increased. The need for high package density for better performance of device and less power consumption can be achieved. The researchers can achieve this by reducing the sub threshold swing (SS) which is limited to 60 mv/dec. Field effect transistors with steep-sub-threshold swing have the potential to lower supply voltage, making them a promising contender for very energy-efficient circuits and systems in the future. The main trade-off is the ambipolar behavior, low on-state current and high miller capacitance of TFETs. When Germanium is used as the source material instead of silicon, a heterojunction forms at source channel junction, and as a effect, an improvised outcome is produced in terms of a steeper subthreshold slope and a lower ION/IOFF ratio. This study analyses transfer properties of negative capacitance tunnel field effect transistors with Si-Source and Ge-Source (NCTFET). Electrical noise analysis and additional AC DC analysis are performed. In this paper, combining these two theories together the recent progress of NC - TFET is discussed.

articleTitle: Investigation of Quantum Ballistic Transport in Single Strand DNA with Silicon Carbide Nanotube: A High performance Embedded System
abstract: DNA has emerged as a strong candidate for nextgeneration ultra-low power applications due to its self-assembly technique. First principle calculations associated with Density Functional Theory (DFT) and Non-Equilibrium Green’s Function (NEGF) analytical method is used for the study of scattered transmission characteristics into the quantum confined DNA strands via Silicon Carbide (SiC) Nanotube (NT) electrodes at 300K. This phenomenon shows that the conductivity of the central molecular region of SiC NT embedded DNA strand has increased and a large number of current flows through the molecular channel. A low HOMOLUMO gap increases the sensitivity of the scattering central molecular channel. The electrical doping process helps to increase the sensitivity of the molecular channel. The sensitivity of the DNA increases satisfactorily.

articleTitle: Graphene Nanoribbon based Triple Barrier Double Quantum Well Resonant Tunneling Diode
abstract: For the first time, we study the characteristic of an all-graphene triple barrier double quantum well resonant tunneling diode structure (TBRTD). The reported results are consistence with the conventional semiconductor based TBRTDs, however, with enhanced structural and functional characteristics. The proposed device shows two negative differential resistance regions in its current-voltage characteristics even at an ultra-compact dimension (63Å× 13.53Å). This opens the window for development of a verity of all-graphene TBRTDs for numerous essential applications such as triple logic memory system, design of THz devices, study of effect of coherence in noise, etc.

articleTitle: Minimally Coupled E-Shaped Dual-band Antenna for Wireless Applications
abstract: A miniaturized ‘E’-Shaped Multi-Input-MultiOutput (MIMO) patch antenna operating at sub-6 GHz for dual-band application is presented in this paper. The antenna covers the two resonating bands at 3.7 GHz (3.5 GHz-3.8 GHz) and 5.7 GHz (5.6 GHz-5.9 GHz) for WLAN applications. Both the resonating bands have more than -20dB return loss. The isolation between the antenna elements is improved by adding ‘C’-Shaped parasitic elements in between the arms of the Eshaped antenna. Incorporating the parasitic patch improves the isolation by 30 dB and 15 dB at the first and second resonant frequencies. A peak gain of 4 dB at 3.7 GHz and 5.2 dB at 5.7 GHz is obtained. optimizing the distance between the MIMO antenna’s radiating elements makes the overall dimension 30\times 29\times 1.6mm<sup>3</sup>. Antenna parameters such as Sparameters, gain, diversity gain (DG), and envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) are measured and found satisfactory for MIMO applications.

articleTitle: 1-bit Magnitude Comparator based on ReversibleLogic using QCA Technology
abstract: The biggest hurdle in today’s processors is heat dissipation. Complementary Metal Oxide Semiconductor (CMOS) is used currently. In CMOS, irreversible computational occurs which leads to heat and energy dissipation. One of the solutions is to use reversible logic. In this paper, a single-bit comparator design is proposed. The device-level implementation of a reversible comparator using Quantum dot Cellular Automata (QCA) is proposed. The design is made using reversible Fredkin and Feynman gates. These are implemented using QCA. Further, the 1-bit magnitude comparator comprised of Feynman and Fredkin gates is designed. In this paper, the device-level reversible logic implementation and energy calculations are claimed although the performance parameters are not that optimized.

articleTitle: High Gain Farming and Data Analytics using IoT
abstract: India is developing exponentially in terms of economy, technology, and innovations but in this race agriculture has left behind. Agriculture was the backbone of the country in terms of production of food, employment and was also boosting the stabilization of population. The GDP contribution of agriculture to the Indian economy was 53% in 1950 and service sector was hanging near 30% but now the figures are completely reversed. According to the economic survey 2020 the GDP contribution of agriculture has dipped to 14% and service sector has seen a hike of 59%. The major reason of difference is the outlook to technology. Service sector has squeezed every drop of available technology weather its IoT, big data or block chain but agriculture never become technology friendly. To increase the GDP contribution, we need to make it a high gain business. So, through this paper our main aim is to merge farming with IoT and data analytics to make it high gain farming.

articleTitle: Augmenting CIGS Solar Cell Efficiency through Optimization of Layer Thickness and Front Electrode Transparency
abstract: This study examines the use of Copper indium gallium diselenide (CIGS) as the active layer of the cell due to its low cost, superior optical properties, low temperature coefficient, direct bandgap, and high stability. The thickness of the active (CIGS) and buffer (CdS) layers have been optimized using SCAPS-ID to achieve the highest power conversion efficiency (PCE). Additionally, the optical transparency of the front electrode has also been examined, and it is found that front electrode transparency should be high (95%) for optimal device performance. The photovoltaic parameters of the cell were found to be: PCE- 16.26%, Voc- 0. 64V, Jsc- 35. 9SmA/cm2 and FF-70.52%.

articleTitle: Statistical Analysis of Integration of renewable DGs in IEEE-9 Bus System using ETAP Simulation
abstract: Due to the hybrid power system’s benefit of integrating renewable energy with the conventional power grid, it is becoming more and more common nowadays. This work provides a thorough statistical analysis of voltage magnitude-based system stability in addition to a description of the composite power system. Using the IEEE-9 bus system, a thorough study of this work has been conducted. The isolated hybrid system that has been presented is comprised a wind turbine and solar PV array to conduct system analysis. The hybrid electric generating station was modeled using the ETAP software tool. In a nutshell, the system behavior on voltage magnitude has been investigated under various cases while incorporating hybrid generation sources by keeping the one conventional generating unit out from the system topology.

articleTitle: Gate-to-Source Leakage Current Computation in Symmetric Double Gate MOSFET incorporating Short Channel Effects
abstract: Gate-to-source leakage current in symmetric double-gate MOSFET is analytically computed considering the effect of transverse surface electric field and surface charges at both the source and drain regions. Tunneling current through trapezoidal potential barrier is considered, and current charge factors are taken into account at both the contacts. Channel length modulation, mobility degradation and threshold roll-off are considered for modelling, and current is computed for various structural parameters and applied bias ranges under practical doping conditions. Optimum lower level of leakage current is identified for specific range of gate bias, and corresponding parameters are also evaluated for best possible performance of the device. Results are useful for applicability in circuit design with lower sub-threshold devices.

articleTitle: Design of a Reliable Copyright Management System Based on Blockchain
abstract: Although data exchange and transparency are encouraged by the Internet, digital information is not protected by it. It has become challenging to publish the Digital Rights Management system in today’s digital environment that can be regarded as well-protected. The value of digital work that is quickly accessible in open-source settings will eventually be zero to the creator. Nonetheless, anyone can download and make copies of content because it is available online. Since the value of data is typically based on how difficult it is to access, the worth of online content gradually declines.It may serve as a good alternative to the aforementioned issues. In this paper, we suggest a blockchain-based approach for a DCM system. In order to keep information transparent and secure, we store thedetails of copyright transactions on the blockchain. Smart Contact replaces the requirement for centralised servers to validate identities and issue licences by ensuring the validity of copyright transactions and issuing licences automatically. The possibility for using blockchain based to address the issue of managing digital copyright. This paper outlines a complete digital copyright management system (DCMS) centred on a public blockchain.

articleTitle: Configurable 8T SRAM-based Computing In- Memory Architecture for Enabling Shift Operation and Multibit Dot-Product Engines
abstract: The conventional computing system in our laptops and mobile phones uses Von-Neumann architecture. Computing In-Memory (CiM) acts as the bottleneck for modern data-intensive applications like artificial intelligence. We have implemented the vector dot-product and shift operation in this work using 8T SRAM for CiM. In order to maintain the precision of a dot-product operation, the cell must be operated in the voltage ranges where the current is a linear function of the applied voltage. We need to size the transistors in the ratio of 8:4:2:1 so that the respective transconductance also remains in the ratio of 8:4:2:1. The summing current of all RBL of four columns yields the required dot product. The left/right shifting operation is implemented with the help of 8T SRAM-based CiM architecture along with a 3×1 multiplexer and D flip flop.

articleTitle: Impact of Doping and Temperature on Mobility in Single and Dual Core S/D GAA FinFETs
abstract: This article proposes a detailed investigation of the dependence of mobility on source(S)/ drain(D) doping concentrations, and temperature in Single Core Gate-AllAround (SC GAA) and Dual Core Gate-All-Around (DC GAA) FinFETs. Four cases of mobility models are considered in the technology computer-aided design (TCAD) simulations. For simpler mobility models like the Masetti model and the Philips Unified Mobility models, the primitive Constant Mobility model is taken as the reference model for computing the drain current sensitivity. For devices where simultaneous presence of (a) Philips Unified mobility model, (b) high-field saturation and (c) mobility degradation (E-normal) model is considered, the devices with simultaneous presence of (a) high-field saturation and (b) mobility degradation (E-normal) models are taken as reference. The sensitivity parameter reveals important conclusions regarding the choice of mobility models.

articleTitle: Gate Engineered IGBT with Improved Device Performance
abstract: Abstract-This article designed silicon carbide (SiC) devices that can be commercially utilized for high power as well as high temperature applications. In this paper, 4 H-SiC-Shielded Trench Gate-IGBT (STG-IGBT) is presented to reduce ON-state voltage drop with capacity of $15-\mathrm{kV}$ blocking voltage. Here, the Silvaco TCAD tool is used to conduct a comparative analysis of the proposed trench device structure with the conventional device structure. According to simulation results, the ON-state voltage drop is reduced by 1.85 % while the breakdown voltages remain approximately the same. The collector voltage of proposed structure is slightly increased by 3.1 % under the condition of 100 $\mathrm{A} / \mathrm{cm}^{2}$ of collector current density and $20 \mathrm{~V}$ of gate voltage.

articleTitle: Slotted Waveguide Antenna for Microwave Remote Sensing Applications
abstract: This article has studied slotted waveguide arrays for use in microwave remote sensing applications. In this study, a conventional dual-frequency slotted waveguide array antenna having dual-linear polarization is considered as a design example and compared with the Dual Frequency SAR antenna, which is a science payload on Chandrayaan-II. The example antenna is optimized to the same operating frequencies of 2.5 GHz (S band) and 1.25 GHz (L band). Results prove that slotted waveguides arrays are suited for modern practical remote sensing applications.

articleTitle: DFT Modeling of a MoS2 Monolayer for C6H12 and C4H8O Detection in Lung Cancer
abstract: In this paper, we have presented the computational study of MoS<inf>2</inf> as a sensing material with the help of density functional theory (DFT) to examine the adsorption and electronic properties, such as band structure, density of states (DOS), adsorption energy, charge transfer and recovery time are examined. Out of many VOCs that are present in lung cancer, here we have focused on only two VOCs i.e., isobutyraldehyde (C<inf>4</inf>HsO) and methylcyclopentane (C$\epsilon \mathrm{H}_{12}$) has been analyzed using MoS<inf>2</inf> material. MoS<inf>2</inf>-C<inf>4</inf>HsO, has the adsorption energy of -0.79eV and 0. 06e charge transfer, and for MoS<inf>2</inf>-$\epsilon$ H<inf>12</inf>, the adsorption energy is -1.13eV and 0. 49e charge transfer. After the adsorption of VOC, the changes in the electronic properties were also observed. These findings suggest that Mo$\mathrm{S}_{2-}\epsilon \mathrm{H}_{12}$ is strongly adsorbed as compared to MoS<inf>2</inf>-C<inf>4</inf>HsO system. Furthermore, the calculated recovery time for C<inf>4</inf>HsO is 22.7 s and 1.2× 10<sup>7</sup>s for C$\epsilon \mathrm{H}_{12}$ at 29S K.

articleTitle: Gate Modulated Graphene Channel TFET with Enhanced Switching Current Ratio
abstract: A single gate modulated graphene channel TFET (GMGCTFET) is proposed. The proposed work is compared with conventional graphene channel TFET (GCTFET) and existing $\mathrm{SiGe}/\mathrm{Si}$ TFET.
